subject: DocuSign routing and countersign timing for AveryCloud DPA
messages:
From: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AveryCloud Legal <legal@averycloud.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA exec flow and signing preferences

Ben —

Thanks for taking this on. We attached our DPA redlines (AveryCloud-DPA-redlines-20280718.pdf). Two quick asks so we can finalize the envelope routing:

1) Can Redwood do parallel signing on DocuSign so our three signers can sign at once, or do you require sequential routing?
2) Will Redwood countersign (CFO) after customer signs, or do you expect both parties to sign and then countersign?
3) We track signer IP + geo for audit — will DocuSign metadata be sufficient, or do you need AdobeSign for EEA audit logs?

Goal: get this executed by next week.

Tom Briggs
Sr. Counsel | AveryCloud
Attachments: AveryCloud-DPA-redlines-20280718.pdf (pdf)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exec flow and signing preferences

Tom —

Quick reply: we support both parallel and sequential envelopes in DocuSign. For most SaaS DPAs we do parallel signing from the customer side and then Redwood performs a single countersignature from our CFO (separate envelope step) to preserve our internal approval flow.

That said, Laura and Finance may need the authority matrix and the signatory names to confirm the countersign path. Monica — can you confirm we have CFO availability for a countersign on 7/24–7/25 if AveryCloud sends the envelope on 7/23?

Also, we generally default to DocuSign for US customers. For EU customers we can switch to AdobeSign if AveryCloud requires additional audit metadata — but often DocuSign is sufficient if we enable signer IP capture + access code.

I attached a short note with proposed envelope settings.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
Attachments: ben_redline-notes-20280719.md (text)

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jul 2028 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exec flow and signing preferences

Ben / Monica / Tom —

Per Redwood execution policy: the standard is customer signatories + Redwood countersign by the CFO or delegated finance signee. We do allow delegation but require the authority matrix to be documented. I attached the current exec-authority matrix for reference (RI-exec-authority-matrix.xlsx).

A few items for the envelope:
- We need the full name, title, and email for each customer signer.
- If AveryCloud will include a PO or SOW reference, include that in the envelope so our Finance team can validate the amount before countersign.
- For cross-border DPAs, please indicate the country of the controller/processor to confirm if SCCs or EU Addendum triggers are needed.

Tom — please share the final signatory list and confirm whether AveryCloud wants parallel routing. If you prefer, we can do a short call Monday to finalize.

Laura Bennett
Head of Legal | Redwood Inference
Attachments: RI-exec-authority-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: AveryCloud Legal <legal@averycloud.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Jul 2028 11:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exec flow and signing preferences

Laura / Ben —

Thanks — attaching our signatory CSV (avery_signatories-20280721.csv). Our preferred flow is parallel signing by the three listed signers (General Counsel, Head of Privacy, Procurement). After those signatures we expect Redwood to countersign (CFO).

A few clarifications:
- We'd like signer IP + geo in the final audit (DocuSign metadata ideally).
- We included a short PO reference in the envelope body.
- On the Subprocessors clause: we prefer a 30-day notice for addition of new subprocessors; is that acceptable?

If DocuSign IP capture works for Redwood, we prefer to keep everything in DocuSign (faster).

Tom Briggs
Sr. Counsel | AveryCloud
Attachments: avery_signatories-20280721.csv (csv)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 14:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exec flow and signing preferences

Tom —

Plan of action:
1) We will prepare a DocuSign envelope configured for parallel signing to the three AveryCloud signers you provided.
2) Envelope authentication: email validation + optional access code per signer (can be enabled on the envelope). Please confirm if you want access codes.
3) Countersign: Redwood CFO will countersign in a follow-up envelope step (we keep customer-signed documents as evidence before countersign). This is our standard to allow Finance validation.
4) DocuSign metadata: we can capture IP, user-agent, and timestamp. For EEA-specific audit fields we can switch to AdobeSign if you confirm that DocuSign metadata is insufficient.
5) Subprocessors: looping Karthik for the recorded process and standard lead time.

Requested next steps from AveryCloud: send envelope by EOD 7/23 (preferred) or confirm alternative date; confirm whether to enable access codes; confirm if you want DocuSign or AdobeSign. Once confirmed we will send our countersign availability window for 7/24–7/25.

Link (placeholder) to envelope settings draft: https://app.docusign.com/envelope/placeholder/ENV-AVY-12345

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Briggs <t.briggs@averycloud.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA exec flow and signing preferences — subprocessors note

Ben / team / Tom —

Quick compliance note on subprocessors: Redwood publishes an up-to-date subprocessor list and provides 30 days' notice for material additions as part of our DPA practice. I attached the current list for transparency (subprocessors-2028-07.csv). For a formal addendum, legal can accept a 30-day notice clause but we don't accept perpetual unilateral approval by the customer. Typical language: 30 days' notice + opportunity to raise objections and (if needed) mitigate via additional controls or SCCs.

On the DocuSign metadata point: DocuSign provides IP/geo + audit trail. If AveryCloud requires signed receipts in a specific EEA-compliant format, we can use AdobeSign on request but that typically slows the timeline by 24–48 hours.

Tom: confirm you want access codes on the envelope and we'll finalize the envelope settings.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessors-2028-07.csv (csv)
